brief.meaningEn: Accept accountability for one’s action, mistake or duty rather than shifting it to others.
brief.meaningZh: 承認自己對行動、錯誤或職責負有責任，而不把責任推給別人。
brief.grammar: Take responsibility for + action/problem; the phrase identifies accountability and can be followed by a specific repair, but does not itself describe the repair.
brief.register: Plain workplace accountability: a project lead tells colleagues she sent the wrong schedule and will correct it.
brief.boundaryZh: 承擔責任不等於獨自造成全部問題，亦不能只靠一句話便證明已完成補救。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是把「責任」當物品拿走，也不是把錯誤全推給下屬。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出應由誰承認自己造成的部分，以及還須採取甚麼具體補救。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 71, row 3; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Leaders should take responsibility for mistakes.

listening.en: The coordinator sent the outdated timetable to families. She said she would take responsibility for the mistake and send a corrected version that afternoon.
listening.zh: 統籌員把舊時間表發給家長。她說會為這次失誤承擔責任，並在當天下午發出修正版。
listening.promptZh: take responsibility 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: She accepts accountability for sending the wrong timetable.
options.zh: 她承認自己發錯時間表的責任。

options.en: She says families caused the mistake.
options.zh: 她說錯誤由家長造成。

options.en: She has already proven every family read the correction.
options.zh: 她已證明每位家長看過修正。

options.en: She can repair the error without telling anyone.
options.zh: 她可不告知任何人便補救錯誤。

listening.explanationZh: 她承認自己發錯版本，並承諾補發。

reply.promptEn: What should the club secretary say after she accidentally omitted two volunteers from the duty list? She prepared the list herself, and the omitted names need adding before tomorrow.
reply.promptZh: （學會秘書不小心把兩名義工漏出值勤名單後應怎樣說？名單由她整理，明天前須補上名字。）

options.en: She should acknowledge that she left the names out.
options.zh: 她應承認自己漏掉名字。

options.en: She can correct the list before it is used.
options.zh: 她可在名單使用前修正。

options.en: She should take responsibility for the omission and update the list.
options.zh: 她應為遺漏承擔責任並更新名單。

options.en: She should not blame the omitted volunteers for her list error.
options.zh: 她不應把自己整理名單的錯誤推給被漏掉的義工。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都把她造成的遺漏與具體修正連起來；金句用 take responsibility。

scene.promptZh: 職員親自把錯誤日期放上網站，發現後向訪客承認並改正。哪句最貼切？

options.en: She took responsibility for the incorrect date and corrected it.
options.zh: 她為錯誤日期承擔責任並作出更正。

options.en: She blamed visitors for reading the date.
options.zh: 她責怪訪客閱讀該日期。

options.en: She denied ever uploading the date.
options.zh: 她否認曾上載日期。

scene.explanationZh: 承認自己上載錯誤並更正，是承擔責任的做法。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個做法最不符合 take responsibility for a mistake？

options.en: The editor admits the wrong caption and publishes a correction.
options.zh: 編輯承認圖片說明有誤並刊登更正。

options.en: The author quietly blames a colleague for an error she herself made.
options.zh: 作者把自己造成的錯誤暗中推給同事。

options.en: The organiser says the invitation omitted the room number and sends an update.
options.zh: 籌辦人承認邀請函漏寫房號並發出更新。

contrast.explanationZh: 把自己造成的錯誤推給同事，是逃避責任。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「她說會 take responsibility，就代表補救已經全部完成。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: Taking responsibility is accepting accountability; we should still check whether the promised correction was sent.
options.zh: 承擔責任是承認應負責任；仍要核實承諾的更正是否已發出。

options.en: A promise to correct proves every recipient already received the new version.
options.zh: 承諾更正就證明每位收件人已收到新版。

options.en: Accountability means the error cannot be corrected.
options.zh: 承擔責任表示錯誤無法更正。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承認責任與完成補救是不同步驟。

speaking.en: I sent the old form, so I will take responsibility for the mix-up and email the corrected link today.
speaking.zh: 我發錯了舊表格，所以會為這次混亂承擔責任，今天電郵發出正確連結。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出說話者承諾的補救。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區活動籌辦人自己發出寫錯集合時間的通知，十位參加者可能受影響；她打算承認失誤並今天發出更正，但仍未確認所有人已收到。用一至兩句英文描述責任和補救狀態。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出錯誤通知由籌辦人發出、她會承擔責任並今天更正、尚未確認所有人收到。

examples.en: The organiser will take responsibility for sending the wrong meeting time and issue a correction today; she has not yet confirmed that all ten participants received it.
examples.zh: 籌辦人會為發出錯誤集合時間承擔責任，今天發出更正；她尚未確認十位參加者全都收到。

examples.en: Because she sent the incorrect notice, the organiser plans to take responsibility for the mistake and send an update today, while receipt by all ten people remains unconfirmed.
examples.zh: 因為錯誤通知由她發出，籌辦人打算為失誤承擔責任，並於今天發出更新；十人是否全都收到仍未確認。

takeaways.en: Take responsibility for a mistake means accept accountability rather than shift blame.
takeaways.zh: 為錯誤承擔責任，是承認應負責而非推卸。

takeaways.en: Taking responsibility is not the same as having completed every corrective action.
takeaways.zh: 承擔責任不等於已完成所有補救。

brief.meaningEn: The reward chosen as the usual first option in a particular setting.
brief.meaningZh: 某個情境中慣常首先採用的獎勵。
brief.grammar: Go-to is a hyphenated adjective before reward; the phrase identifies a habitual default, not the only reward ever used.
brief.register: Reflective classroom planning: a teacher tells a colleague that praise has become her routine response to effort and considers when other feedback might help.
brief.boundaryZh: 慣常首選不等於永遠唯一，亦不證明它對每位學生都最有效。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是「走到獎勵那裏」；一次使用還不足以稱為 go-to。
brief.outcomeZh: 能根據反覆選用的證據辨認預設獎勵，同時保留例外及效果評估。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 74, row 9; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Praise became the go-to reward in the classroom.

listening.en: For months, the teacher has praised pupils first whenever they show effort; she uses stickers only occasionally. Praise has become her go-to reward.
listening.zh: 幾個月來，老師每逢學生用功，通常先給口頭讚賞，貼紙則只偶爾使用。讚賞已成為她的慣常首選獎勵。
listening.promptZh: go-to reward 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: Praise is her usual first reward for effort.
options.zh: 讚賞是她獎勵用功時慣常的第一選擇。

options.en: She has used praise only once this year.
options.zh: 她今年只讚賞過學生一次。

options.en: Stickers are the only reward she ever gives.
options.zh: 貼紙是她唯一會給的獎勵。

options.en: Every pupil prefers praise to every other form of feedback.
options.zh: 每位學生都比起任何其他回饋更喜歡讚賞。

listening.explanationZh: 她幾個月來反覆先用讚賞，貼紙只是偶爾使用。

reply.promptEn: Why does the sports coach call a short thank-you note his regular choice? After almost every volunteer shift he writes one; certificates are reserved for occasional milestones.
reply.promptZh: （體育教練為何說簡短感謝卡是他的慣常選擇？幾乎每次義工值勤後，他都寫一張；證書只在偶爾的重要節點頒發。）

options.en: He gives thank-you notes after most shifts.
options.zh: 他在大多數值勤後送感謝卡。

options.en: Certificates remain available for special milestones.
options.zh: 證書仍可用於特別的重要節點。

options.en: A note is his go-to reward for regular volunteer help.
options.zh: 感謝卡是他獎勵日常義工幫忙時的首選。

options.en: His usual acknowledgement is a note, not a certificate.
options.zh: 他慣常以感謝卡而非證書表達謝意。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都據頻率判斷首選獎勵，沒有排除證書；金句用 go-to reward。

scene.promptZh: 社區中心幾乎每次孩子完成閱讀任務都讓他們選一本二手書，只有少數日子改送書籤。哪句最貼切？

options.en: A second-hand book is the centre’s go-to reward for the reading task.
options.zh: 二手書是中心給完成閱讀任務孩子的慣常首選獎勵。

options.en: The centre has offered a book only once.
options.zh: 中心只曾送書一次。

options.en: The centre never gives any bookmarks.
options.zh: 中心從不送書籤。

scene.explanationZh: 反覆送書而偶爾送書籤，支持「慣常首選」。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個證據最不足以稱一項獎勵為 go-to reward？

options.en: A tutor chooses it after nearly every completed practice session.
options.zh: 導師幾乎每次學生完成練習都選它。

options.en: A school gives it once for a unique anniversary and never again.
options.zh: 學校只在一次獨特周年活動頒發，之後沒有再用。

options.en: A club usually offers it first, with occasional alternatives.
options.zh: 學會通常先給這項獎勵，偶爾改用其他。

contrast.explanationZh: 只用過一次，不足以構成慣常首選。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「這是老師的 go-to reward，所以每個學生都一定喜歡，而且她不能用其他獎勵。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: It is her go-to reward because she chooses it often; that does not prove universal preference or exclude alternatives.
options.zh: 它是慣常首選，因為她經常使用；這不證明人人喜歡，也不排除其他選擇。

options.en: A default reward must be every pupil’s favourite.
options.zh: 預設獎勵一定是每位學生最喜歡的。

options.en: If she ever uses another reward, there cannot be a go-to choice.
options.zh: 只要她曾用其他獎勵，就不可能有首選。

dialogue.explanationZh: 使用頻率與普遍喜好是兩回事，首選也容許例外。

speaking.en: The club’s go-to reward for regular helpers is a handwritten note, while an annual certificate marks exceptional service.
speaking.zh: 學會對日常幫手慣常首選的獎勵是手寫感謝卡，年度證書則表揚特別傑出的服務。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說出兩種獎勵的使用頻率。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：圖書館閱讀計劃通常在孩子完成一本書後送書籤，偶爾在學期末送證書；負責人仍在評估書籤對不同孩子是否有效。用一至兩句英文描述慣常獎勵與限制。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出書籤是反覆使用的首選、證書只是偶爾發、效果仍待評估，不要說每個孩子都喜歡。

examples.en: A bookmark is the library’s go-to reward when a child finishes a book; certificates are occasional, and staff are still checking how well bookmarks work for different children.
examples.zh: 孩子讀完一本書時，書籤是圖書館慣常首選的獎勵；證書偶爾才發，員工仍在評估書籤對不同孩子的效果。

examples.en: The programme usually gives a bookmark after each finished book, making it the go-to reward; end-of-term certificates are rarer, and its effect for every child is still being assessed.
examples.zh: 計劃通常在孩子讀完一本書後送書籤，使它成為慣常首選獎勵；學期末證書較少發，而書籤對不同孩子的效果仍在評估。

takeaways.en: A go-to reward is the usual first choice, not the only reward available.
takeaways.zh: 慣常首選獎勵是通常先選的，不是唯一可用的獎勵。

takeaways.en: Calling something a go-to reward does not show it works for everyone.
takeaways.zh: 稱一項獎勵為慣常首選，不代表它對每個人都有效。

brief.meaningEn: A short, intense moment of enthusiasm, often after a particular trigger.
brief.meaningZh: 因某件事而出現的短暫強烈興奮。
brief.grammar: A burst of excitement is a noun phrase, often follows bring/cause/feel; it identifies a temporary reaction, not lasting satisfaction.
brief.register: Warm but measured activity report: a teacher describes pupils’ immediate reaction to a surprise game without claiming the whole programme succeeded.
brief.boundaryZh: 短暫興奮不代表長期喜愛或活動一直成功；須看其後反應。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是實際爆炸，也不是平穩持續整天的情緒。
brief.outcomeZh: 能說出引發短暫情緒的事件，並把當下反應與長期效果分開。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 75, row 4; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: The new game brought a burst of excitement.

listening.en: When the new game began, the room filled with cheers for a few minutes. It brought a burst of excitement, though the pupils soon returned to their quiet projects.
listening.zh: 新遊戲開始時，教室歡呼了幾分鐘。它帶來一陣興奮，但學生很快又回到安靜的專題活動。
listening.promptZh: a burst of excitement 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: A brief, strong enthusiastic reaction to the game.
options.zh: 對遊戲短暫而強烈的興奮反應。

options.en: The pupils stayed equally excited for the entire week.
options.zh: 學生整個星期都保持同等興奮。

options.en: A physical explosion occurred in the room.
options.zh: 教室發生了實際爆炸。

options.en: The game was proven to improve all later projects.
options.zh: 遊戲已證實能改善所有後續專題。

listening.explanationZh: 歡呼只持續幾分鐘，之後活動恢復平靜。

reply.promptEn: What happened when the orchestra announced a surprise guest? The audience cheered loudly for a minute, then settled down to listen to the rehearsal.
reply.promptZh: （樂團公布驚喜嘉賓時發生甚麼事？觀眾高聲歡呼約一分鐘，然後安靜下來聽綵排。）

options.en: The announcement briefly stirred strong enthusiasm.
options.zh: 公布消息短暫引起強烈興奮。

options.en: The audience cheered and then settled.
options.zh: 觀眾歡呼後便安靜下來。

options.en: There was a burst of excitement after the surprise announcement.
options.zh: 驚喜公布後，現場出現一陣興奮。

options.en: The reaction was vivid but did not last through the rehearsal.
options.zh: 反應熱烈，但沒有持續整場綵排。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出短暫強烈反應；金句用 a burst of excitement。

scene.promptZh: 科學隊收到入圍通知，歡呼十秒後又繼續工作，最後得獎與否尚未定。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The notice brought a burst of excitement, but the final result remains open.
options.zh: 通知帶來一陣興奮，但最終結果仍未確定。

options.en: The team has already won the final award.
options.zh: 團隊已拿到最終獎項。

options.en: Their excitement lasted without pause all day.
options.zh: 他們一整天都持續興奮。

scene.explanationZh: 入圍令他們短暫興奮，不等於已獲最後獎項。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不足以說 a burst of excitement？

options.en: A surprise visitor prompts a minute of delighted applause.
options.zh: 驚喜訪客引起一分鐘開心掌聲。

options.en: A group remains mildly interested at the same level for six months.
options.zh: 小組六個月都保持相同程度的輕微興趣。

options.en: A winner’s name triggers sudden cheers that quickly fade.
options.zh: 公布得獎者時突然歡呼，然後很快平息。

contrast.explanationZh: 平穩持續的輕微興趣，缺少短暫而強烈的反應。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「孩子見到新遊戲時很興奮，所以這課程日後一定長期成功。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: The game brought a burst of excitement, but lasting interest needs separate evidence.
options.zh: 遊戲帶來一陣興奮，但能否維持興趣須另有證據。

options.en: One lively minute guarantees long-term learning.
options.zh: 一分鐘熱烈反應保證長期學習成效。

options.en: A short cheer means nobody enjoyed the game.
options.zh: 歡呼短暫代表沒有人喜歡遊戲。

dialogue.explanationZh: 短暫反應不能直接證明長期成效。

speaking.en: The announcement of a surprise exhibit brought a burst of excitement before visitors returned to the guided tour.
speaking.zh: 驚喜展品公布時帶來一陣興奮，之後訪客繼續導賞。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出興奮何時出現及持續多久。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：博物館宣布下月會展出一幅罕見畫作，現場觀眾歡呼約一分鐘，然後繼續聽原本的講座；展覽尚未開幕，也未有參觀滿意度資料。用一至兩句英文描述反應及限制。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出宣布引起約一分鐘強烈興奮、講座繼續、展覽尚未開幕；不要當作長期成功證據。

examples.en: The rare-painting announcement brought a burst of excitement: visitors cheered for about a minute, then returned to the talk; the exhibition has not opened yet.
examples.zh: 罕見畫作公布時引起一陣興奮：訪客歡呼約一分鐘，然後繼續聽講座；展覽尚未開幕。

examples.en: Visitors showed a burst of excitement and cheered for about a minute when the museum named next month’s exhibit, then returned to the talk; the exhibition has not opened, so later satisfaction is unknown.
examples.zh: 博物館公布下月展品時，訪客興奮歡呼約一分鐘，然後繼續聽講座；展覽尚未開幕，日後滿意度仍未明。

takeaways.en: A burst of excitement is intense but brief.
takeaways.zh: 一陣興奮是強烈而短暫的。

takeaways.en: A burst of excitement does not by itself prove lasting success.
takeaways.zh: 短暫興奮本身不證明長期成功。

brief.meaningEn: Prefer fewer well-made or useful things to a larger number of weaker ones.
brief.meaningZh: 寧取較少但更好、更有用的東西，不只追求數量多。
brief.grammar: Quality over quantity is a compact principle often used as a noun phrase or stand-alone judgement; the quality criterion must be stated in context.
brief.register: Practical curriculum planning: a library coordinator tells tutors why three well-supported workshops may serve children better than twelve rushed sessions.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是「少就一定好」；要有具體質素差異，亦不表示數量永遠不重要。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是把可行的大規模服務一概排除，也不能只減少數目卻不改善內容。
brief.outcomeZh: 能比較具體品質與數量取捨，並說明選較少的理由。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 75, row 7; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: For toys, quality over quantity is sensible.

listening.en: The toy shop offered two sturdy puzzles that children could use repeatedly instead of a box of twenty flimsy prizes. The parent chose quality over quantity.
listening.zh: 玩具店有兩款耐用、孩子可反覆玩的拼圖，也有一盒二十件易壞的小獎品。家長選擇重質不重量。
listening.promptZh: quality over quantity 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: The parent preferred fewer durable toys to many weak ones.
options.zh: 家長寧選較少但耐用的玩具，而非多件易壞品。

options.en: The parent chose the box solely because it contained more pieces.
options.zh: 家長只因盒內件數多而選它。

options.en: Every small set is automatically better than every large set.
options.zh: 任何小套裝都一定勝過任何大套裝。

options.en: The puzzles were chosen without any quality comparison.
options.zh: 家長選拼圖時完全沒有比較品質。

listening.explanationZh: 選擇依據是耐用與可反覆使用，不只是數量少。

reply.promptEn: Why did the art club choose four coached sessions instead of twelve five-minute demonstrations? Pupils could practise and get feedback in each coached session, while the short demonstrations allowed neither.
reply.promptZh: （藝術學會為何選四節有導師指導的活動，而非十二節五分鐘示範？學生可在每節有指導的活動中練習並獲回饋，短示範則兩者都做不到。）

options.en: The four sessions offered practice and feedback.
options.zh: 四節課提供練習與回饋。

options.en: The club valued useful depth above session count.
options.zh: 學會重視有用的深度多於節數。

options.en: The choice put quality over quantity.
options.zh: 這項選擇重質不重量。

options.en: The shorter demonstrations could not meet the stated learning need.
options.zh: 簡短示範無法滿足所述學習需要。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以練習和回饋的品質解釋較少節數；金句用 quality over quantity。

scene.promptZh: 雜誌可刊兩篇經充分核實的專訪，或十篇未核對資料的短文；編輯選前者。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The editor put quality over quantity by choosing two checked interviews.
options.zh: 編輯選兩篇已核實專訪，是重質不重量。

options.en: The editor chose ten unchecked pieces to maximise volume.
options.zh: 編輯選十篇未核對短文，以提高數量。

options.en: Two pieces are always superior even when their facts are wrong.
options.zh: 兩篇文章即使事實有錯，也總勝過其他選擇。

scene.explanationZh: 兩篇有查核，十篇未查核，質素差異有具體根據。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個做法最不支持 quality over quantity？

options.en: A team publishes three tested guides instead of fifteen untested drafts.
options.zh: 團隊刊出三份測試過的指南，而非十五份未測試草稿。

options.en: A club cuts ten useful sessions to two equally rushed ones without improving them.
options.zh: 學會把十節有用課縮成兩節同樣匆忙的課，沒有改善內容。

options.en: A charity chooses one reliable helpline with trained staff over several unstaffed numbers.
options.zh: 慈善機構選一條由受訓職員接聽的可靠熱線，而非幾條無人接聽的電話。

contrast.explanationZh: 單純減少數量而沒有提高質素，不能算重質不重量。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「只要變少，就一定是 quality over quantity。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: Quality over quantity needs a real quality gain, such as better practice or feedback, not just fewer items.
options.zh: 重質不重量要有真正質素提升，例如更好的練習或回饋，不只是數目減少。

options.en: Any smaller number automatically means better quality.
options.zh: 任何較小數目都自動代表較高質素。

options.en: The phrase means number never matters in any decision.
options.zh: 片語表示任何決定都不用考慮數量。

dialogue.explanationZh: 選較少須有具體品質理由，而非以少為本。

speaking.en: We chose quality over quantity: three small workshops with individual feedback instead of twelve crowded talks with no practice.
speaking.zh: 我們選擇重質不重量：三節小組工作坊有個別回饋，而非十二場擠迫又無練習的講座。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出質素改善在哪裏。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：圖書館暑期閱讀計劃可開三節由受訓導師帶領、每位學生能獲回饋的工作坊，或十二節沒有練習與回饋的匆忙講座；小組選前者，但仍需預留足夠名額。用一至兩句英文解釋取捨。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出三節有導師和回饋、十二節欠缺練習、小組仍須確保足夠名額；不是少就一定好。

examples.en: The library chose quality over quantity: three tutor-led workshops with individual feedback instead of twelve rushed talks without practice, while still reserving enough places.
examples.zh: 圖書館選擇重質不重量：開三節有導師指導和個別回饋的工作坊，而非十二節缺乏練習的匆忙講座，同時仍預留足夠名額。

examples.en: Three coached workshops give pupils practice and feedback that twelve rushed talks cannot; the library put quality over quantity but will check that enough children can join.
examples.zh: 三節有指導的工作坊讓學生練習及獲回饋，是十二節匆忙講座做不到的；圖書館選擇重質不重量，但仍會確認足夠孩子可參加。

glossary.zh: 三節有導師指導的工作坊

takeaways.en: Quality over quantity prefers stronger outcomes, not merely a smaller count.
takeaways.zh: 重質不重量是追求較好效果，不是單純減少數目。

takeaways.en: Choosing quality over quantity can still require enough places for the people served.
takeaways.zh: 重質不重量時，仍可能要確保服務對象有足夠名額。

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent English, Chinese, media and QA review remain pending. Source is guide-written provenance; practice scenes are newly written. No human or release approval is implied.
